text:
Alice Chen: Morning handoff — wrapping up my day shift. I'm the primary until 2026-03-15 07:00 UTC (thread root). Secondary is Rohit. Quick snapshot of coverage: APAC night gap between 02:00-04:00 UTC where we only have on-call overlap if someone volunteers.

Rohit Patel: Ack. I can extend to 03:30 UTC if needed. Maya — can you cover 03:30 onward? Otherwise we need a volunteer from infra.

Maya Torres: I can pick up from 03:30 to 07:00 UTC. Confirming access checklist now.

Alice Chen: Checklist for whoever is primary/secondary, please confirm each item before claiming primary: 1) PagerDuty - able to view and acknowledge alerts for the redwood-prod service and incident escalation policy, 2) AWS - can assume role `redwood-oncall` and access CloudWatch/SSM session-manager for instances, 3) Grafana - can view `prod-inference-ops` dashboard and inspect traces, 4) Runbooks - can open the runbook and follow mitigation steps.

Samir Khan: Adding one more: alerting pages page should show your phone/email in PD. If mobile push fails, make sure PD has your fallback contact.

Maya Torres: Quick audit results — PD ok (can see redwood-prod), AWS OK except I don't have `sts:AssumeRole` for `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-oncall` (SSO denies me), Grafana viewer OK.

Rohit Patel: I just ran the PD check — I can see alerts but not the escalation policy details (read-only limited). Grafana shows me as `Editor`. AWS assume-role works for me.

Alice Chen: If you hit the AWS assume-role error, try the CLI to get the error text and screenshot for infra ticket:```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-oncall --role-session-name oncall-check
```

Alice Chen: If Grafana is missing, infra usually grants `Viewer` on the `prod-inference-ops` folder. PagerDuty access requests go through the access pipeline (okta -> PD groups) — quick steps in runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/oncall-access-requests (link internal).

Samir Khan: If anyone is missing PD access and it's urgent (can't ack pages), DM me and I'll escalate to Security SSO to fast-track. Otherwise file an access request and cc `#infra-access` and `#oncall` with the ticket id.

Rohit Patel: One small gotcha we found yesterday: Grafana panels that use Loki/tempo require the `logs-view` role in addition to dashboard viewer. If you can't view traces, check that role.

Alice Chen: Thanks — note for handoff: please run this quick pre-handoff test (takes ~3 mins):
1) Ack a test alert in PD (we use the test service `redwood-test-alerts`).
2) Run AWS assume-role command above.
3) Open https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/prod-inference-ops and expand the top right trace panel.
4) Open runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/prod-inference/mitigation and confirm you can follow step 2 (roll back route).

Maya Torres: Completed steps 1–3, failed step 2 earlier but retested and infra fixed `sts:AssumeRole`. All good now.

Alice Chen: Coverage gap note — we only have one person who can perform emergency DB failover (RDS) during 02:00-03:00 UTC; if an incident requires that, we need Samir on-call or exec approval to proceed. Marking this as a risk for the night.

Samir Khan: Acknowledged. I'm on standby for failover but prefer to avoid unless SLOs are violated. If triggered, follow runbook section "DB emergency failover" and inform `#exec-oncall`.

Oncall Bot: Automated access audit — Alice: PD=ok, AWS=ok, Grafana=ok; Rohit: PD=ok(read-limited), AWS=ok, Grafana=editor; Maya: PD=ok, AWS=ok(after fix), Grafana=viewer.

Alice Chen: Handoff complete. I'm passing primary to Rohit at 07:00 UTC (timestamped). Rohit — say "take" when you are primary. Otherwise I'll remain until confirmed.

Rohit Patel: take. I'm primary. Maya secondary. Leaving a note: if you need to request access mid-shift, use `#infra-access` with subject: "oncall access request" and include your Okta email + missing resource. Keeps ticket triage fast. :thumbsup:

Alice Chen: Thanks all — logging this handoff to the night Handoff board and adding the APAC gap as a risk. End of thread.
